title: Rothko show in Florence - Marginal REVOLUTION
gist: Cowen reports from Florence on the Palazzo Strozzi Rothko show and its San Marco satellite exhibit, arguing the Fra Angelico juxtaposition exposes Rothko as fundamentally a religious painter, and notes two side observations: an outsized share of Chinese visitors, and that August Florence is unexpectedly tolerable because overtourism elsewhere has equalized crowding.

insights.claim: Hanging smaller, lighter-colored Rothkos beside Fra Angelico frescoes at Museo San Marco reveals Rothko to have been fundamentally a religious painter rather than a secular abstractionist.
insights.speaker: Tyler Cowen
insights.so_what: A reframing of Rothko's canon as devotional art supports the durability of his blue-chip valuation, since religious/transcendent framing broadens the collector base beyond mid-century modernism specialists.
insights.quote: Those rooms bowled me over, as for one thing they show how much Rothko was a religious painter at heart.
insights.locator: In Museo San Marco there is an ancillary exhibit

insights.claim: The Palazzo Strozzi Rothko retrospective opens with a room tying early Rothko works directly to Renaissance art, a curatorial choice Cowen flags as surprising.
insights.speaker: Tyler Cowen
insights.so_what: Major institutions repositioning a modernist as an heir to Renaissance devotional painting is the kind of narrative shift that precedes re-rating in the top end of the art market.
insights.quote: The main Rothko show, at Palazzo Strozzi, had an opening room showing Rothkos tied to Renaissance (!) art, mostly with works from early Rothko.
insights.locator: The main Rothko show, at Palazzo Strozzi

insights.claim: Chinese visitors made up an unusually high proportion of attendees at the Florence Rothko exhibit even though Chinese tourists are not especially numerous in Florence at present.
insights.speaker: Tyler Cowen
insights.so_what: Disproportionate Chinese turnout for Western postwar abstraction is a leading indicator of where marginal demand for high-end Western art and cultural travel is coming from.
insights.quote: I also was struck by the high proportion of Chinese visitors at this show, even though they are not especially numerous in Florence right now.
insights.locator: I also was struck by the high proportion

insights.claim: Ken Griffin owns Rothko works of high quality, one of which is on loan to the Florence exhibition.
insights.speaker: Tyler Cowen
insights.so_what: Billionaire-financier collections increasingly supply museum-grade loans, tightening the float of trophy Rothkos available to the market.
insights.quote: Ken Griffin has very good taste in Rothko.
insights.locator: Ken Griffin has very good taste

insights.claim: Visiting Florence in August is now less unpleasant than expected because crowding has spread so widely to other destinations that Florence's summer congestion no longer stands out, and the heat itself deters visitors enough that restaurants have no dinnertime crush.
insights.speaker: Tyler Cowen
insights.so_what: Universal overtourism erodes the premium on off-peak timing; the tradable version is that heat-deterred peak-season slots in famous cities are now the cheap seats.
insights.quote: So many other places have become crowded that the situation here does not phase me.
insights.locator: Visiting Florence in August is less unbearable
